headline: Ramp, a company that sells corporate cards and expense software, raised $1.85 billion at a $60 billion valuation, up from $44 billion in June.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a very large round and a sharp jump in four months; revenue figures are the company's own.
importance_line: Shows investors still paying heavily for software that adds AI to company spending and finance work, which affects finance teams at its 85,000 customers and older rivals; revenue and growth figures are Ramp's own.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by Central Oregon Daily, that Ramp said it raised $1.85 billion in a round led by Dragoneer Investment Group at a $60 billion valuation, up from $44 billion in June. Ramp says it makes more than $2 billion in annualized revenue, is cash-flow positive and serves more than 85,000 companies, and it is adding tools that monitor what firms spend on AI.
notes: Read via Central Oregon Daily, which carries the Reuters text.
